messages:
infra-bot: [ALERT] elevated NVIDIA Xid 13 rate on eu-west1 A10 pool (past 10m) — 62 events across 8 racks. auto-tagging #eng-sre
Ashwin: seeing the spike, pulling telemetry now. can we get top tenant breakdown?
Maya: initial observation: many events line up with sustained NIC receive rates. looks like heavy small-packet bursts overlapping GPU busy windows.
Jess: do we have host logs showing "GPU fallen off the bus"? that usually points at PCIe/nvlink flaps.
ops-sre: pasted dmesg excerpt from host eu-w1-r03-host7:
```
[34567.123456] NVRM: Xid (13): 79, Ch 00000000, engine 00000100
[34567.123457] NVRM: GPU at 0000:af:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[34567.123458] nvlink: link after reset
```
Ashwin: good catch. I ran a quick DB query: `SELECT tenant_id, count(*) FROM gpu_xid_events WHERE xid=13 AND region='eu-west1' GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 6;` top is tenant-42 (embedder bursts), then tenant-77 and a few infra test jobs.
Maya: tenant-42 rolled a batch change yesterday (batch_size: 8 -> 32) on their embedder. timeline aligns with start of spike.
Sienna: I'm the SE for tenant-42 — confirming they ramped batch and started higher concurrency. they've paused the ramp after our ping.
Jess: recommended immediate steps: 1) soft-drain affected GPUs, 2) divert new tenant-42 traffic to standby pool, 3) ask tenant to revert batch while we triage.
ops-sre: starting soft-drain on affected GPUs in racks r03, r07, r22 at 15:09 UTC.
Ashwin: I'll add a temporary route override: `route set tenant-42 -> eu-west1-standby` so new sessions avoid the hot pool.
infra-bot: route update applied for tenant-42 at 15:11:24 UTC. auto-fallback policy set to re-evaluate after 10m of normal xid rate.
Maya: PROM slices to capture: `gpu_kernel_latency`, `nic_rx_bytes_total`, `xid_count{xid=\"13\"}`, `nvlink_errors_total` for 14:45-15:20 UTC. saving queries.
ops-sre: after soft-drain Xid count dropped from 62 -> 7 in 9m. remaining events are spread across unrelated racks.
Ashwin: hypothesis: high small-packet NIC RX combined with long-running decode kernels produces PCIe stalls or driver-level timeout -> Xid 13. NVLink reset entries in dmesg support transient link issues. ECC counters look nominal.
Jess: any sign of Xid 31 or 48 during the window? those would point to memory/thermal or firmware issues.
Maya: Xid 31 appears 3 times on separate hosts that later showed nvlink re-negotiation. no 48 in this incident.
Sienna: tenant-42 rolling back batch_size to 8 for 2 hours and applying client-side rate limiting. they'll monitor via their dashboards and report back.
ops-sre: we performed a controlled powercycle on eu-w1-r03-host7 after persistent Xid post-drain. nv_persist logs uploaded: s3://infra-logs/1743314567/host7-nvpersist.tar.gz
Ashwin: action items for follow-up: - correlate nvlink/PCIe resets + NIC RX peak + tenant request patterns; - collect driver logs/versions; - schedule targeted driver micro-patch to eu-west1 A10 pools next week behind canary; - implement temporary tenant caps for embedder batch_size for 24h.
Maya: I'm building a short dashboard snippet for the postmortem: will include the exact SQL and Prom queries and overlay of tenant-42 traffic frequency.
Jess: impact estimate: ~3-4% capacity offline while drains completed. cost delta small vs risk. Ops, please notify billing of temporary standby usage.
infra-bot: incident record created: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1743314567
ops-sre: monitoring looks stable after the mitigations. closing active response — leaving mitigation flags for 24h.
Ashwin: assigning postmortem author: Ashwin. PM draft due EOD tomorrow. include mitigation timeline, exact commands, and nv_persist artifacts.
Sienna: will confirm tenant-side telemetry and share traces if anomalies persist. thanks for the quick coordination.
Jess: thumbs up. reopen thread if we see recurrence. :thumbsup:
